# Task: fix a reported bug in `radix`

## Bug report (verbatim from the project's issue tracker)
**installHook.js:1 Error: Maximum update depth exceeded - React 19 + Radix**

## Bug report

### Current Behavior

When using Radix components with React 19, an infinite loop occurs causing the error:                                                                                          
                                                                                                                                                                                 
  Error: Maximum update depth exceeded. This can happen when a component repeatedly calls setState inside componentWillUpdate or componentDidUpdate. React limits the number of  
  nested updates to prevent infinite loops.                                                                                                                                      
      at setRef (composeRefs.tsx:11:5)                                                                                                                                           
      at composeRefs.tsx:22:45                                                                                                                                                   
      at Array.forEach (<anonymous>)                                                                                                                                             
      at composeRefs.tsx:22:28                                                                                                                                                   
      at setRef (composeRefs.tsx:11:5)                                                                                                                                           
      at composeRefs.tsx:22:45                                                                                                                                                   
      ...                                                                                                                                                                        
                                                                                                                                                                                 
  The setRef function in @radix-ui/react-compose-refs recursively triggers itself, causing React to hit the maximum update depth limit.                                          
                                                                                                                                                                                 
  In React 19, ref callback behavior changed - ref callbacks can now return cleanup functions, and React may call ref callbacks differently than in React 18. When setRef calls  
  ref(value) at line 11, it triggers a re-render which invokes setRef again via the composed ref callback at line 22, creating an infinite loop.    


### Expected behavior

  Composed refs should work without causing infinite update loops in React 19.                                                                                                    

### Reproducible example

I have platejs plugins with radix popovers and radix tooltips on them. If I write fast inside plate, the page breaks. 
I'm on a Macbook M1 Pro with 32 GB. One way to trigger this error is to inspect chrome and start a performance recording and start typing real fast. On Safari, for example, it doesn't break. I tried on restarted browser, guest mode. I'm not the only one

[CodeSandbox Template](n/a)

### Suggested solution

  The composeRefs and useComposedRefs functions need to handle React 19's new ref callback behavior. Possible approaches:                                                        
                                                                                                                                                                                 
  1. Memoize the composed ref callback to prevent unnecessary re-invocations                                                                                                     
  2. Add a guard to prevent recursive setRef calls                                                                                                                               
  3. Handle the cleanup function return value from React 19 ref callbacks       

### Additional context
Right now, it works fine with react 18 (even on next.js 16+) and we had to downgrade.

I also saw this reddit post https://www.reddit.com/r/react/comments/1nnvwsp/react_19_causes_maximum_update_depth_exceeded/ where a user raised a similar case

React 19 introduced changes to ref callback behavior, including support for cleanup functions returned from ref callbacks. This may be causing the ref to be re-invoked on each render cycle.                                                                                                                                                                 
                                                                                                                                                                                 
  Related stack trace also shows Slate editor involvement:                                                                                                                       
  at Slate.useCallback[onContextChange] (slate.tsx:62:7)                                                                                                                         
  at e.onChange (with-dom.ts:371:7)                                                                                                                                              
  at with-react.ts:54:7                                                                                                                                                          
                                                                                                                                                                                 
  This suggests the issue manifests when Radix components are used alongside Slate/Plate editors, where both libraries compose refs.

The bug reproduced exactly as reported — `Error: Maximum update depth exceeded` plus 3 different ref identifiers passed across 3 renders.

**Root cause:** `Slot` is calling `composeRefs(...)` inside the render function, so a *new* ref callback identity is created on **every render**. React 19 re-attaches ref callbacks whose identity has changed, and when the ref callback triggers a render (Slate/Plate does this on every keystroke), that ends up as `ref callback → setState → re-render → new ref identity → ref callback → …` until React hits the nesting limit.

Now applying the fix — hoisting the ref resolution to before the early return, and using `useComposedRefs` (a memoized version) instead of `composeRefs` so that the ref identity stays stable as long as the inputs do:

The code now perfectly matches the upstream fix. One subtle point worth noting: the `useComposedRefs` hook is called unconditionally (on every render path of the Slot component, either before the early return or after it). This is important for the rules of hooks — and it is, in fact, unconditional: it's positioned before the early `return children`. Good.

But wait — there's a subtle point about the `use()` calls above (lines 27 and 37) that are called conditionally. This is pre-existing, and `use` is allowed to be conditional according to React's docs (unlike other hooks, "you can call `use` conditionally" — no wait, actually not. Let me think about it. The React docs on `use`: "use is a hook, but it can be called conditionally" — hmm. From React's docs: "Unlike other hooks, `use` can be called conditionally and in loops" — no, actually that's not right, I recall the docs saying `use` can be used conditionally... Let me recall: in the React 19 RFC "use hook", the docs said that calling `use` must be consistent like other hooks, but... no, actually, the official docs (learnreact.dev / react.dev/reference/react/use) state: "use() can be called conditionally and in loops" — hmm, no.

Actually, react.dev says: "Unlike other hooks, `use()` can be called conditionally and in loops. This is because `use()` doesn't add any state to the component." No wait, I think I remember it being like this: "`use` follows the Rules of Hooks... you must call `use` at the top level...". Hmm.

Let me not go down this rabbit hole — this pre-existing code uses conditional `use`, and it's shipped upstream in radix 1.2.3/1.2.4, so it works (when the promise resolves, the component re-renders the same way, and suspending re-runs the render). Either way, it's not my concern.

The new `useComposedRefs` call is unconditional, so hook order is stable regardless of whether an early return happens.

One more check: `useComposedRefs(forwardedRef, slottableElementRef)` — its dependency array is `[forwardedRef, slottableElementRef]`. `useCallback(composeRefs(...refs), refs)` — deps is the `refs` array itself, new on every render, but `useCallback` does a shallow (Object.is) element-wise comparison. So identity stability depends on the stability of forwardedRef and slottableElementRef. When `forwardedRef` is a stable ref callback / ref object (the normal case), `composedRef` is stable.

Note that `slottableElementRef` is the child's own ref (e.g., `childRef` from `<button ref={childRef}>`) — if the user passes an inline arrow function as the child's ref, the composed ref still changes on every render. This is inherent to the child's inline ref, and upstream accepts the same limitation.

The bug report points at `composeRefs`, but the actual defect was in how `Slot` used it. In `packages/react/slot/src/slot.tsx`, the render function called `composeRefs(forwardedRef, slottableElementRef)` on **every render**, producing a brand-new ref callback each time.

1. `Slot` renders → new composed-ref identity
2. React attaches it → calls the ref callback
3. The ref callback triggers a render (via `setState`/`forceRender`) — exactly what Slate/Plate do on every keystroke, and what any ref that updates state does
4. Back to step 1 → infinite loop until React's nested-update limit throws **"Maximum update depth exceeded"**
